policies.title: United States: Canadian citizen visitor-visa exception
policies.summary: Canadian citizens generally do not require a visa for temporary visitor travel to the United States.
conditions: This policy is limited to Canadian citizens seeking ordinary temporary visitor admission; it is not a rule for Canadian permanent residents or other nationals travelling on a Canadian-issued document.
Under 8 CFR 212.1(a)(1), a visa is generally not required for Canadian citizens, but E, K, S, and V nonimmigrant classifications remain exceptions.
A valid unexpired passport is generally required, subject to the regulation's limited NEXUS, FAST, SENTRI, Canadian-Indian, and child-document exceptions.
Visa-free documentary treatment does not guarantee admission; the traveller remains subject to inspection and admissibility requirements.

policies.title: United States: Bahamian visitor visa exception at Bahamas preclearance
policies.summary: A Bahamian national may receive the regulation's narrow visitor visa exception only after satisfying a U.S. immigration officer in the Bahamas before or at embarkation.
conditions: A passport is required.

The exception applies only when, before or at embarkation by vessel or aircraft, the traveller satisfies the examining U.S. immigration officer in the Bahamas that the traveller is clearly and beyond doubt otherwise entitled to admission under INA section 212(a).
This is not a general visa-free rule: the regulation otherwise requires a visa for Bahamian nationals, including travel not qualifying for the Bahamas inspection exception.
This policy does not cover British subjects resident in the Bahamas who lack Bahamian nationality.

policies.title: United States: Compact of Free Association citizen nonimmigrant entry
policies.summary: Eligible Compact of Free Association citizens of Micronesia, the Marshall Islands, and Palau may apply for U.S. nonimmigrant admission without visas.
conditions: For Micronesia and the Marshall Islands, the USCIS fact sheet identifies citizens by birth and specified former Trust Territory citizens who acquired the relevant citizenship as entitled to this Compact treatment.
For Palau, the USCIS fact sheet identifies citizens by birth and specified former Trust Territory citizens who acquired Palau citizenship in 1994 as entitled to this Compact treatment.
Admission is not guaranteed; U.S. inadmissibility grounds, including criminal grounds, still apply.
This is a Compact-based nonimmigrant status, not a finding that every holder of a travel document issued by these countries is eligible.

policies.title: United States: Mexican visitor visa or Border Crossing Card
policies.summary: Mexican citizens seeking ordinary U.S. visitor admission generally need a nonimmigrant visa; the DSP-150 Border Crossing Card is a combined B-1/B-2 visitor visa document.
conditions: The Border Crossing Card is a B-1/B-2 visitor visa, not a visa-free entitlement.
A Border Crossing Card is issued only to applicants who are citizens of and resident in Mexico, who meet B-1 and/or B-2 eligibility standards and plan to stay no more than six months.

Under 8 CFR 212.1(c), a Mexican temporary visitor from Mexico at a land port, pleasure vessel, or ferry may use a biometric DSP-150; specified rules also govern use with a passport from other than contiguous territory.
Crew, official-passport, and Kickapoo-document provisions in 8 CFR 212.1(c) are outside this ordinary-passport visitor policy.

policies.title: United States: People's Republic of China visitor visa and EVUS condition
policies.summary: A People's Republic of China passport holder seeking ordinary visitor admission requires a B-1, B-2, or B-1/B-2 visa; holders of the specified 10-year visas must also maintain EVUS enrollment.
conditions: The Department of State says Chinese citizens with 10-year B-1, B-2, or B-1/B-2 visas in People's Republic of China passports must update EVUS every two years, or after a new passport or qualifying visa.
EVUS is an additional travel condition for the specified visa holders; it is not a substitute for a visitor visa.
A visa permits travel to request entry but does not guarantee admission, which CBP decides at the port of entry.

policies.title: United States: ordinary visitor visa cohort outside documented nationality exceptions
policies.summary: For the listed ordinary-passport nationalities, temporary business or tourism travel to the United States requires a B-1, B-2, or B-1/B-2 visitor visa, subject to individual eligibility and admission decisions.
conditions: This policy concerns ordinary-passport visitors temporarily travelling for business (B-1), tourism (B-2), or both (B-1/B-2); it does not classify work, study, residence, crew, transit, diplomatic, official, refugee, or other non-visitor routes.

The cohort is the complement, within the repository's ordinary passport catalog, of the VWP/ESTA cohort documented in the separate existing candidate, Canadian and narrow Bahamas exceptions, Compact of Free Association citizens, Mexican BCC treatment, People's Republic of China EVUS treatment, and U.S. citizens.
A visa application is individual: applicants must establish eligibility under U.S. law, and a visa permits travel to request entry rather than guaranteeing admission.
Returning U.S. lawful permanent residents use permanent-resident travel documentation rather than a B visitor visa; this policy does not classify them by their other nationality.
The Guam-CNMI Visa Waiver Program is a distinct, territory-limited program and is not used to classify entry to destination code US in this policy.
Case-specific passport or visa waivers, including unforeseen emergencies, do not establish a nationality-wide ordinary visitor exception.

policies.title: United States: U.S. citizen entry-document scope
policies.summary: A U.S. citizen is not a foreign visitor-visa applicant; CBP publishes U.S.-citizen documentary requirements for return to the United States.
conditions: This policy is limited to U.S. citizens and does not establish requirements for dual nationals travelling as foreign visitors.
CBP requires a valid U.S. passport for U.S. citizens entering by air, with different listed document options for land or sea travel.

conflicts.explanation: The fallback snapshot uses a flat visa-required status. 8 CFR 212.1(a)(3) creates a narrow visa-free Bahamas preclearance exception but otherwise requires a visa; the flattened status needs reviewer judgment.
